heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 describe the executed program of proof.md section 9 under the stated rules: 1 per field operation (a Montgomery conversion is one multiplication), 1 per element load or store plus 1 address operation, 3 per loop iteration plus 2 per loop exit (the loops written with the macro FOR8 are unrolled eight times in the source and charged 3 per pass of eight; the generated kernels are straight-line), 1 per other executed index or control operation, 300 per reduced permutation evaluation, and a register file of 18 words of 256 bits per transform block (16 data words plus two working words: the twiddle operand and the butterfly temporary) as the only register assumption; the allocator (`xalloc`, `xfree`) is charged per executed operation, and the report formatting, the single write and the exit are charged in stage I. The run used 6 threads: each thread counts its own operations, the main thread sums them, the loop control of a split loop is charged once, and the thread control (10,000 operations per futex or clone system call, 1,000 per woken worker, small constants per dispatch and chunk) is charged on top and listed in the THREADS line (proof.md section 4.5). The best-case recount of proof.md section 10 re-prices this same executed run under a single-trial single-thread (T=1) precommitted schedule and two declared stacked levers (CRT transform de-padding; stage-D degree-1-certifying truncated half-gcd), each an exact arithmetic reduction of the section 6 stage totals; the memory placement of section 10.4 is a credited derivative of 0xshikhar 52120fad.
